thread_analysis.thread_summary: Move Corporation (contact Koji Kishimoto), a prospective customer in an extended information-gathering phase before committing to any specific product registration, engages Allion (Kentaro Taniguchi, Itsuo Sakai) for general Bluetooth SIG certification consulting, spanning March through May 2025. The thread is unusually dense with generalizable rules rather than project-specific execution: free derivative registration mechanics, the selling-company-vs-manufacturer registration axis, a comprehensive design-change decision tree, ICS detail viewing, and finally a transition into scoping an actual headphone product registration once the customer's understanding solidified.
all_questions_found: Is Bluetooth certification needed per model name, or is it tied to the underlying qualification with free derivative additions available? (see thread_0040_case_01)
Does a manufacturer change versus a selling company change affect Bluetooth registration validity differently, and how does this differ from Japan's radio-law rule? (see thread_0040_case_02)
Does an electrically-identical product rebranded under a different selling company qualify for any reduced-cost registration path? (see thread_0040_case_03)

Which categories of design change (non-Bluetooth SoC features, antenna/RF circuit changes, non-antenna circuit changes, enclosure changes) require a new registration, a free derivative addition, or no action at all? (see thread_0040_case_04)
How can detailed, layer-by-layer ICS content be viewed for an example registration, and why might the relevant link appear missing? (see thread_0040_case_05)

For an actual headphone product registration using an already-qualified module, what does 'measurement data' refer to, what does it cost, and how does Declaration fee payment and Receipt Number timing work? (see thread_0040_case_06)
(Administrative, not separately cased) Scheduling coordination for phone calls and clarification follow-ups -- routine project administration without a generalizable technical lesson.
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: This thread is exceptionally rich in generalizable, reusable consulting content rather than project-specific execution detail, since it captures an extended pre-registration education phase. Case_04's comprehensive design-change decision tree is the standout contribution, cleanly separating four distinct change categories (non-Bluetooth SoC features, antenna/RF circuit, non-antenna circuit, enclosure/housing) with different consequences for each, including the subtle Power-Class-boundary trigger for antenna changes. Case_02 and case_03 together form a complete picture of the selling-company-identity axis that governs Bluetooth registration validity, contrasted explicitly against Japan's manufacturer-identity-based radio-law regime.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: See thread_0040_case_01 through thread_0040_case_06 for case-specific decision logic; the throughline is that Bluetooth SIG registration scope and validity are determined by specific, well-defined axes (selling company identity, registered Power Class, Bluetooth Support Layer/ICS content, Conduction-Mode-only testing) that often surprise customers more familiar with adjacent regulatory regimes (like Japan's radio law) operating on different axes (manufacturer identity, Radiation Mode testing).
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: See individual case files; case_04 carries the broadest risk given its many distinct sub-rules, particularly the Power-Class-boundary trigger for antenna changes, which could be missed if a customer assumes any antenna change qualifies for free derivative addition.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: No significant consulting-side mistakes identified -- the consultant's responses were thorough, used concrete examples (the Raytac MDBT module ICS walkthrough) to ground abstract explanations, and proactively flagged subtle exceptions (the Power Class boundary case) rather than giving oversimplified answers.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When a prospective customer is in an extended pre-registration information-gathering phase, invest in thorough, example-grounded explanations of the underlying rules (registration scope, the selling-company axis, the design-change decision tree) since this front-loaded education reduces friction once the customer transitions to an actual product registration, and proactively distinguish Bluetooth SIG's specific rules from adjacent regulatory regimes (like national radio law) that customers may incorrectly assume follow the same logic.
